questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today?
options: They have greater ambitions than their parents.
They find it difficult to achieve upward mobility.
They have overtaken their parents in terms of earnings.
They envy the opportunities in other industrialised nations.

questions.q: What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows in America?
options: They reinterpret the essence of the popular rags-to-riches culture.
They urge people to achieve economic success through hard work.
They help strengthen people’s conviction in the American Dream.
They feature ordinary Americans striving for social recognition.

questions.q: What does the author say about news broadcasts in America?

They are bent on reporting the dark side of life.
They stand in striking contrast with reality TV.
They focus on Americans’ economic hardships.

questions.q: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general?
